entry.label: Lineage recovery
entry.description: The evidence-led practice of recovering neglected people, traditions, institutions and transmissions while stating whether the relation is authorship, teaching, collaboration, appropriation, exclusion, canonisation or later rediscovery.
entry.canonical_definition: The evidence-led practice of recovering neglected people, traditions, institutions and transmissions while stating whether the relation is authorship, teaching, collaboration, appropriation, exclusion, canonisation or later rediscovery.

profile.summary: Lineage recovery finds and types neglected transmissions without turning every resemblance, shared identity or later citation into influence.
profile.canonical_definition: Lineage recovery finds and types neglected transmissions without turning every resemblance, shared identity or later citation into influence.
profile.why_it_matters: It makes the history of visibility part of the atlas rather than treating omissions as empty space around an otherwise neutral canon.
common_misreadings: Recovery is not achieved by adding portraits to an unchanged structure.
Shared heritage is not evidence of conceptual influence.
open_checks: Develop gold-standard examples of exclusion, appropriation, canonisation and recovery with page-level evidence.

connections.scope_conditions: This is an atlas practice connection, not a claim that one named author originated lineage recovery.

connections.source_locator: Public editorial requirement and systems-thinkers boundary article
connections.scope_conditions: The practice does not presume every absence is an exclusion; it investigates the history and relation type.

sources.title: The Necessary Tangle running feedback: canon, closure and patriarchy
sources.notes: Public curator note recording the challenge about a predominantly white male visual canon and the resulting editorial requirement to expose canonisation, exclusion, appropriation and recovery rather than repair the map through portraits alone.
